newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African retirement fund tax changed in budget.
newsitem.headline: S.African retirement fund tax changed in budget.

text.p: Finance Minister Trevor Manuel on Wednesday announced several detailed changes to tax regulations covering the retirement fund industry.

He said income received by retirement funds from property unit trusts and from borrowers would be subject to 17 percent tax from March 1 while lump sum benefits paid to members by public sector retirement funds would be subject to tax from March 1.

A 17 percent tax was imposed on the interest and rental income of retirement funds last year and Manuel said that no further major changes would be made until present negotiations through the national retirement fund consultative forum had been completed.
"There are, however, some aspects that require further attention," he said.

When funds invested in property unit trusts, for example, they received dividends from property companies. These were effectively a distribution of rental income but were not currently subject to tax.
"Given that such dividends effectively represent rental income, they will be subject to the tax on retirement funds with effect from March 1, 1997," Manuel said.
In addition, the interest or fees paid by borrowers on loans from retirement funds would also be taxable from March 1.
Manuel said these two measures would yield 200 million rand in additional revenue.

He also announced that members of public and private sector retirement funds would receive equal tax treatment from March 1. Previously, only members of private sector funds had to pay tax on lump sum benefits but this would now also apply to public sector fund members.
This would, however, be subject to the protection of vested rights in terms of the number of years of service and final salary.

Manuel said that the government was "extremely concerned" about the way in which medical savings schemes and other types of "salary sacrifice" schemes were being used to reduce taxable income and these were being investigated.
